clue.text: Severn phenomenon that fails to generate interest?

definitions.meaning: the tidal wave that surges up the River Severn estuary each spring tide
a tedious person or thing that leaves everyone uninterested

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a river wonder that somehow leaves onlookers unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Severn, in western England and Wales, has a famous tidal surge travelling upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a tidal surge up an estuary, and a tedious person or thing.

clue.text: Brown box sitting on upturned cask

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a chest is a large box

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word for cask is read from the bottom

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

explanation.surface: A brown box perched on top of an overturned barrel, like a cellar scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' turns TUN into NUT beneath CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut is a reddish-brown colour, named after the nut's shell.

clue.text: Flat, as revealed by map, overlooking a river

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece above looks over what comes below it

parts.note: a plan is a map or drawing of an area

explanation.surface: A map shows that the land beside a river is flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar is a geometric term for lying in a single plane, i.e. level and two-dimensional.

clue.text: Separating English and US agents participating in swindle

indicators.note: the agents take part within the swindle, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: An English officer and American agents split up while taking part in a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Segmenting is dividing into parts, a synonym for separating.

clue.text: Revolutionary with fate sealed beginning to shred garments

indicators.note: the fate is sealed up inside the revolutionary, enclosed by his name

parts.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary
one's lot is one's fate

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A doomed revolutionary starts tearing up clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are items of clothing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Panic — a festival needs these places for refreshment

indicators.note: the run of words needs the answer in the sense of containing it within its letters

explanation.surface: Organisers fret that a festival must provide food stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' signals that the answer runs across the end of 'Panic', all of 'a', and the start of 'festival'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafes are small eateries where people stop for drinks and snacks.

clue.text: Reports most agitating about soldiers, assault forces

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the soldiers, enclosing them
stirring up the letters of the words reports most into a new order

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: News reports alarm people about troops being sent in as attack forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitating' shuffles REPORTS MOST into STORMTRPES-style letters that 'about' wraps around OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormtroopers are specially trained shock troops used to lead an attack.

clue.text: Alien has this extra rest

parts.note: the word Alien holds the word ... it, between A and N, and that phrase is also a long morning in bed

explanation.walkthrough: Split the clue's first word as A-LIE-N: it has LIE inside it. Read that observation as a phrase and it means an extra spell in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A late morning spent in bed is extra rest beyond one's usual sleep.

clue.text: Name of woman that's a little granny, one might surmise?

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
the French-derived suffix -ette marks something small, as in kitchenette

explanation.surface: Guessing at a woman's name that sounds like a pet name for a small grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived diminutive suffix marks smallness, as in kitchenette; the question mark admits the name is not really derived this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a female given name, a diminutive of Anne.

clue.text: Leaving with Her Majesty's presents

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, and the possessive adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone departs carrying gifts belonging to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; here the 's supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Offers as a verb means puts forward or presents something for acceptance.

clue.text: Gold label at the front of books for decoration

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the books in the answer

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a name is a label given to something
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A gilt label on the cover of books serves as a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is an object or flourish added purely for decoration.

clue.text: Star no more after explosion? That interests me

definitions.text: Star no more after explosion? That interests me

indicators.note: the words are blown apart and their letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A sky-watcher remarks that a star which has gone supernova fascinates them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a supernova leaving a star no more is exactly what fascinates such a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer studies celestial bodies, so a dying star is of professional interest.

clue.text: Farm animal needing restraint, liable to collapse?

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shackle is a fetter or restraint

explanation.surface: A sheep that needs tethering because it keeps falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle describes a building so badly made or kept that it looks about to fall down.

clue.text: What some unfortunately have in their hair, idiots!

definitions.text: What some unfortunately have in their hair
definitions.meaning: the eggs of head lice found on scalps
fools, as in British slang nitwits

explanation.walkthrough: Short for nitwits, this is British slang for fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice eggs stuck in hair, and a colloquial insult for stupid people.

clue.text: A mere idealist forced to disappear

indicators.note: the letters are forced out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreamy idealist is made to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: To dematerialise is to lose physical form and vanish, as in science fiction.

clue.text: Illustration of Indian city, dingy on the outside

indicators.note: the word for dingy sits around the city, enclosing it

parts.note: dim means poorly lit or dingy
Agra, home of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A picture of an Indian city looking gloomy round its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simplified drawing used as an explanatory illustration.

clue.text: Hand out drink — see cat dipping into it

indicators.note: the pair go down into the drink, ending up inside it

parts.note: ale is beer
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Pour a drink, then watch the cat dunk itself in it.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the archaic 'behold', a crossword stand-by for 'see'.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to distribute or apportion shares, i.e. to dole things out.

clue.text: Mess food?

definitions.meaning: a dish of chopped meat and potato fried together

explanation.walkthrough: Mess also suggests a military dining hall, tying both senses together.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a muddle of something is a jumble, and a fried dish of chopped leftovers shares the word.

clue.text: Degenerate academic left one by entrance

indicators.note: placed beside, the entrance comes next

parts.note: prof is short for professor
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an entrance through a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A dissolute professor left someone waiting at the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate is a dissolute, wasteful person; degenerate as a noun means the same.

clue.text: Adaptable factory once head of industry gets stuck in

indicators.note: the letter is lodged inside the word for factory

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A works that was once a leader of industry has adapted to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means flexible and easily bent, so readily adaptable.

clue.text: Sign of approval about hospital being very friendly

indicators.note: the approval mark is placed round the hospital letter

parts.note: a tick is the mark showing something is correct
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A thumbs-up for a hospital that treats patients warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick' as in 'thick as thieves' means close or intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick, informally, means intimate or close, as with close companions.

clue.text: Performance is given energy after pair warm up?

indicators.note: the performance comes after the pair in the answer

parts.note: an act is a stage performance
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stage act gets livelier once a double act has warmed up the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that warming up is only one example of rehearsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming up before an event is a form of rehearsal or drilling a skill.

clue.text: Firm joins US university engaging a thousand in effect

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the university takes on the thousand, holding it inside

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A company teams up with an American university that hires a thousand staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to carry it out or perpetrate it, the verb sense of perpetrating an act.

clue.text: Nothing about which fellow gets to complain

indicators.note: the fellow goes about, i.e. around, the zero

parts.note: a man is a fellow or chap
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man grumbles about receiving nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to grumble or whine, a synonym for complain.

clue.text: Chaps eating half the bread and fruit

indicators.note: the chaps take the piece into themselves, holding it inside

parts.note: men are chaps

indicators.note: only the first two of the four letters of the bread word are kept

explanation.surface: Men tucking into half a loaf with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large, juicy fruit of the gourd family.

clue.text: Upset group given support

parts.note: a set is a group of things
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A team distressed after receiving encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal of fortune, and an upset as a noun means the same.
